{"kind":"ready","manifest":"960bfad7f31f9b9a6d67b81f6c38aab15fa2cbd2278dcbe49ad106215e6fd012","artifact":"c40b6f9d7fe3b24cc7e739eab7c31bb4d34717aaf9fb67cce2ef4eee55ee6020","result":"e2c67eb65a86a6fc0e8a3c7ad6a0520db41a2e121a36426a1899200f4fb3631f","receipt":"41f49fe60972bbf31ec079e1619af7cc5340e705ca0a835907ef8f3fc32b46b7","key":"L3:integrated-change-impact","scope":"session-input","title":"L3:integrated-change-impact","layer":3,"need":"flow","navigation":["L1:authority","L1:entry-execution","L1:identity","L1:promotion-reuse"],"dependencies":["L2:component-admission","L2:component-projection","L2:component-delivery","L2:component-execution"],"body":"## Consequences and boundaries
| Change category | Coupled obligations to assess |
|---|---|
| `equivalent`, delivery default, ID generation, `resume` wake condition | Receipt identity, conflict conversion, wake advisory, and projection matching; widening equivalence accepts conflicting reuse, narrowing it turns context/time-differing retries from equivalent to conflicting — E-AD lines 36-36, 47-49; E-PJ lines 32-32, 45-45. |
| Row fields, indexes, `admittedSeq`/`promotedSeq` assignment, `projectPrompted` update/fallback/insert | Pending vs promoted/visible state, fallback insertion setting both sequences, and timing of `run(db, event)` after `Prompted` — E-PJ lines 21-26, 40-40, 45-49; E-AD lines 30-32, 51-51. |
| Context/time/promoted-sequence checks in `matchesProjection` | Historical and duplicate projection acceptance; shrinking it to `equivalent` could admit rows that fail the existing projection comparison, depending on the mismatched fields and path; the existing-row fallback acceptance and the update-path gate must be assessed separately, not treated as a guaranteed non-matching promotion — E-PJ lines 34-34; E-AD lines 30-30. |
| Cutoff capture, steer ordering, earliest-queue selection, one-row queue limit, continuation/idle reevaluation | Which pending rows are promoted in a turn and in what order; cutoff-qualified steers and earliest queued selection have different predicates and must not be unified without changing eligibility — E-DL lines 20-22, 34-34; E-PJ line 27. |
| Pre-promotion checks, intended vs observed allowance reset, step-limit logic, `MAX_STEPS_PROMPT` insertion relative to transform | Whether rows remain pending, allowance accounting, and request content; insertion after transformation would no longer match the inspected order, but alone does not prove a specific input survives or fails in a request — E-DL lines 26-28, 34-34. |
| `run`/`wake` branches, drain eligibility, pending-wake consumption, Session-ID keying, Location placement | Join/start/coalesce, process-local scope, and whether admitted input becomes visible; coordination change does not by itself prove serialization, cross-process ownership, or provider completion — E-EC lines 18-20, 32-32, 36-36. |

A behavior-preserving change (e.g., internal refactoring that preserves the predicates, carriers, cutoff/queue predicates, insertion order, and wake branches above) is an interpretation grounded in those contracts, not an automatic contract violation. An intentional contract change requires an explicit decision on the affected predicate or carrier and re-assessment of the coupled rows in the table. Not every implementation edit necessarily fails a supplied test; a hypothetical change is not proof that a specific test fails — E-AD lines 47-52; E-DL line 34; E-EC line 32. No rationale, provider exactly-once, crash-recovery, hosted/distributed, or cross-process guarantee is invented — E-AD lines 15-15, 55-55; E-PJ lines 42-42, 51-51; E-EC lines 24-28.
